question: What is the main goal of using skull traction for someone with a neck injury?

options.A: To align and stabilize damaged cervical vertebrae
options.B: To completely replace the need for future spinal surgery
options.C: To deliver intravenous pain medication directly to the neck
options.D: To increase blood flow to the brain tissues

explanation: You've got this! Skull traction gently pulls to put broken or dislocated neck bones back into place and keeps them steady so they can heal safely. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why is skull traction chosen over a soft neck collar for severe fractures?

options.A: It applies skeletal-level pulling force to overcome strong neck muscles
options.B: It requires no monitoring by nursing staff after the initial setup
options.C: It completely eliminates all risks of developing a wound infection
options.D: It allows the patient to get out of bed and walk around freely

explanation: Think about how strong neck muscles are! A soft collar is too weak for bad fractures, but skull traction uses weights to pull against those tight muscles and fix the bones. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which of these is the most common reason a patient needs skull traction?

options.A: Degenerative arthritis of the lumbar spine

explanation: Spot on! Traction is specifically built to handle broken bones and bad misalignments right in the neck area. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h2)

question: How does pulling the neck bones back into alignment help the spinal canal?

options.A: Seal cerebrospinal fluid leaks inside the neck
options.B: Speed up the healing of torn skin tissues
options.C: Prevent the patient from developing a respiratory infection
options.D: Relieve pressure on the spinal cord by creating space

explanation: Great thinking. When the bones snap back into their correct spot, it opens up the spinal canal and takes dangerous pressure off the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is the name of the popular skull traction device that uses spring-loaded pins?
explanation: Gardner-Wells tongs are super common in the ward. They use clever spring-loaded pins to rest safely on the sides of the head. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is a huge plus of wearing a halo vest compared to lying flat in bed with tongs?

options.A: It allows the patient to sit up and move around safely
options.B: It completely removes the need for pin site cleaning
options.C: It does not require any pins to penetrate the skull bone
options.D: It applies continuous heavy weight without using pulleys

explanation: Halo vests are amazing because they attach the head ring to a body vest, meaning the patient isn't stuck flat in bed all day! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h3)

question: What type of medication is given to the scalp right before placing traction pins?
explanation: A local anesthetic is injected right where the pins will go so the patient stays completely numb and comfortable. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h4)

question: A scared patient asks if the metal pins will hurt going into their head. What should you say?

options.A: You will feel a sharp pain, but it will go away as soon as the weights are hung.
options.B: Do not worry, the pins are very small and just rest on top of your hair.
options.C: Most patients are asleep during the whole process so they never feel anything.
options.D: The doctor will numb your scalp with medicine first so you won't feel sharp pain.

explanation: Always be honest and comforting! Letting them know the doctor will numb the area first builds great trust and calms their nerves. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h4)

question: Where must the traction weight bags always be positioned?

options.A: Tied tightly to the metal headboard of the bed
options.B: Supported on a small stool placed next to the bed
options.C: Resting securely on the bottom mattress for safety
options.D: Hanging freely without touching the floor or bed frame

explanation: Spot on! If the weights rest on the floor, the pulling force stops, and the patient's neck bones could shift out of alignment. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h5)

question: A visitor bumps the bed and a weight bag touches the floor. What is your very first step?

options.A: Immediately remove the skull pins to prevent further injury
options.B: Document the incident and wait for the doctor's morning round
options.C: Call the physical therapist to readjust the entire bed frame
options.D: Ensure the rope is in the pulley and lift the weight so it hangs freely

explanation: Quick action is key! Just check the rope and make sure those weights are hanging freely again to keep the traction working. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the main risk of having metal pins go through the scalp into the skull bone?

options.A: Permanent hair loss across the forehead
options.D: Complete loss of the sense of smell

explanation: Anytime the skin is broken by metal pins, bacteria can sneak in, making infection our top worry to watch out for. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h6)

question: During pin site care, why should you avoid scrubbing away dried crusts around the pins?

options.A: Crusts are needed to hold the metal pin tightly in place
options.B: Crusts act as a protective barrier against bacteria
options.C: Scrubbing crusts will cause the traction weights to fall off
options.D: Dried blood keeps the patient's scalp warm and dry

explanation: Hands off those crusts! They actually act like a natural little shield protecting the healing skin underneath from germs. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h6)

question: What bad thing can happen if you put way too much weight on a skull traction setup?

options.A: Over-distraction that can tear spinal ligaments
options.B: Rapid healing of the bone without any scars
options.C: Complete paralysis of the facial muscles
options.D: Immediate closure of the patient's airway

explanation: Too much of a good thing is bad! Pulling too hard stretches the spine too far apart and can actually tear the delicate ligaments. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h7)

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when responding to a cardiac arrest in a patient with skull traction?

options.A: Keeping the neck in neutral alignment during all emergency maneuvers
options.B: Ensuring a doctor or emergency team member manages the head position
options.C: Removing the traction weights immediately to start chest compressions
options.D: Following hospital guidelines for emergency airway management

explanation: Never just yank the weights off in a panic! Removing them suddenly can cause the injured neck to snap out of place. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T11#GNS221_U1_T11_h7)
